security_spec.violation_condition: When XiangShan's CSR execution unit implements CSRRS/CSRRC as a read-modify-write sequence on pmpaddr CSRs, the read phase returns the 'read as' (grain-masked) value for bits [G-1:0] instead of the underlying stored value. During the subsequent write-back, these bits — now read as 0 — are written back as 0, clobbering the underlying stored value even though rs1 did not target those bits. The SILENT-META pmps are in the process of refactoring, this issue should be properly considered based on the current state of the pmps.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: pmpaddr CSR read path returning grain-masked value during CSRRS/CSRRC read-modify-write; write-back path using the masked read result rather than preserving underlying bits whose read representation differs from stored value; CSR module performing true atomic RMW without distinguishing 'read as' from 'underlying' bit values for pmpaddr[n][G-1:0]
security_spec.summary: XiangShan CSRRS/CSRRC read-modify-write on pmpaddr silently corrupts grain-masked address bits — stored 1 bit reads as 0 and gets written back as 0, enabling hardware-level PMP bypass without the attacker touching the grain field
